q: A cheetah is fast. A snail is the opposite of fast. Which word fits the snail?
why: Opposites mean the reverse. Quick means almost the same as fast, so it cannot be the opposite.
hint: Opposite means the reverse.

q: Which word rhymes with 'whale'?
why: Whale and tail end with the same sound. Wheel starts like whale but ends differently.
hint: Listen to the ending sounds.

q: Put 'moon' and 'light' together. What new word do you make?
why: Two small words can join into one compound word. Keep them in order: moon, then light.
hint: Keep the two words in the same order.

q: The word 'rocket' has two syllables (claps).
why: Rock-et has two claps. Each syllable has one vowel sound you can hear.
hint: Clap the word out loud.

q: The dinosaur was huge. Which word means almost the same as huge?
why: Huge and giant both mean very big. Tiny means the opposite.
hint: Pick the word that also means very big.

q: In 'The shark swims fast,' which word is the action word?
why: Swims tells what the shark does, so it is the verb. Shark is the who, and fast tells how.
hint: Which word shows something happening?

q: Put these baseball words in ABC order.
why: Look at the first letter of each word: b, g, p, u. That is the order of the alphabet.
hint: Check the first letter of each word.

q: Which word begins with the same sound as 'shark'?
why: The letters sh make one sound. Ship starts that way. Sun starts with s alone, and chip starts with ch.
hint: Say 'shark' slowly and listen to the start.

q: One beach, two ____. Which plural is spelled right?
why: Words that end in ch, sh, s, x, or z add -es to mean more than one.
hint: Say it out loud with two beaches.

q: 'Octo' means eight. An octopus has that many arms. How many arms is that?
why: Octo means eight, and an octopus does have eight arms. An octagon has eight sides too.
hint: The answer is hiding in the question.

q: Last night we ____ at the stars. Which word fits?
why: Last night already happened, so the verb needs -ed. Looked tells about the past.
hint: Last night is over. Use the past form.

q: Which sentence asks a question?
why: A question asks something and ends with a question mark. The other two tell or shout.
hint: Look for the question mark.

q: 'Swimmed' is the right word for what a shark did yesterday.
why: Swim changes to swam in the past. Some verbs do not follow the -ed rule.
hint: Say it in a sentence: Yesterday the shark ...

q: A diver swims down in deep water. Which word is the opposite of deep?
why: Deep water goes far down. Shallow water is not deep, so you can stand in it.
hint: Think of water you can stand in.

q: Shark, whale, and ____ all live in the sea. Which word fits?
why: A dolphin is a sea animal like the others. A robin is a bird, and a camel lives in the desert.
hint: Which animal lives in the ocean?

q: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
why: A sentence starts with a capital letter, tells who or what, then what it does.
hint: Start with the word that has a capital letter.

q: Shark starts with S. Which letter comes right before S in the alphabet?
why: The alphabet goes Q, R, S, T. R comes right before S, and T comes right after.
hint: Sing the alphabet song up to S.

q: Which word is spelled the same forward and backward?
why: Wow reads the same both ways. Wolf backward spells flow. Words like wow are called palindromes.
hint: Read each word from its last letter.

q: A shark isn't a mammal. Which two words make 'isn't'?
why: The apostrophe takes the place of the o in not. Is not squeezes into isn't.
hint: Which letter does the apostrophe replace?

q: 'Mars spins.' is a complete sentence.
why: A complete sentence tells who or what, and what it does. Mars is the who, and spins is the action.
hint: Does it tell who and what they do?

q: Which word sounds just like 'whale' and means a long, sad cry?
why: Wail and whale are homophones: they sound alike but have different spellings and meanings.
hint: Find the word that sounds the same as whale.

q: One wolf, two ____. Which plural is spelled right?
why: Many words that end in f change to -ves in the plural. Leaf becomes leaves, and wolf becomes wolves.
hint: Say 'two wolves' out loud.

q: Sam's bat is long. Leo's bat is longer. Pat's bat is the ____ of all.
why: Use -er to compare two things. Use -est to compare three or more things.
hint: Count how many bats are being compared.

q: The words 'huge' and 'tiny' are synonyms.
why: Synonyms mean the same thing. Huge and tiny mean opposite things, so they are antonyms.
hint: Do the two words mean the same or opposite?

q: The coach said the call was unfair. What does 'unfair' mean?
why: The prefix un- means not. Unfair means not fair.
hint: Think about what the prefix un- does.

q: A diver who has no fear is called ____.
why: The suffix -less means without. Fearful means full of fear, which is the opposite.
hint: Which word ending means without?

q: Put the word parts in order to spell a baseball position.
why: Out + field + er spells outfielder, a player who catches balls far from home plate.
hint: Think of the grassy part of the field.

q: Which word is NOT a compound word?
why: Sunshine is sun + shine. Seahorse is sea + horse. Seal is one word, not two small words joined.
hint: Try splitting each word into two real words.

q: Shark skin feels rough when you rub it one way. Which word is the opposite of rough?
why: Smooth means even, with no bumps. It is the opposite of rough. Sharp and rocky are different ideas.
hint: Think of something with no bumps.

q: The comet zoomed through the sky. Which word means almost the same as zoomed?
why: Zoomed means moved very fast. Raced means almost the same. Floated is slow, and stopped is not moving.
hint: Picture how fast a comet moves.

q: How many syllables (claps) are in the word 'triceratops'?
why: Tri-cer-a-tops has four claps. Clap once for each beat as you say it slowly.
hint: Say it slowly and clap each beat.

q: A bat flew out of the cave at dusk. In this sentence, what does 'bat' mean?
why: Bat can mean the animal or the stick in baseball. The cave and flew are clues. A bat is a mammal, not a bird.
hint: Use the clues cave and flew.

q: Please ____ the score on the board. Which word fits?
why: Write means to put words or numbers on a surface. Right means correct or the opposite of left.
hint: Which word means putting marks on a board?

q: The word 'ocean' is a noun.
why: A noun names a person, place, or thing. Ocean names a place.
hint: Nouns name people, places, or things.

q: ____ octopus has eight arms. Which word fits?
why: Use an before a word that starts with a vowel sound. Octopus begins with the short o sound.
hint: Does octopus start with a vowel sound?

q: The past tense of 'grow' is 'growed'.
why: Grow changes to grew in the past. Irregular verbs do not follow the -ed rule.
hint: Say: Yesterday the baby shark ... bigger.

q: In 'The slippery eel hid,' which word is the adjective?
why: An adjective describes a noun. Slippery tells what the eel is like. Hid is a verb.
hint: Which word tells what the eel is like?

q: The crab scurried across the sand. What does 'scurried' mean?
opts: rested quietly in the warm sun
dug a very deep hole in sand
why: Scurried means ran fast with short, quick steps. Crabs often scurry sideways.
hint: Picture a crab hurrying across a beach.

q: In the baseball word 'knuckleball', the letter k is silent.
why: The k is silent in knuckleball, just as in knee and knot. You say 'nuckleball'.
hint: Say the word aloud and listen for a k sound.

q: Add -ing to 'swim'. Which spelling is right?
why: In short words with one vowel and one ending consonant, double the consonant before -ing.
hint: Listen to the short i sound in swim.

q: The coach and the umpire could not agree. Which word means 'to not agree'?
why: The prefix dis- means not or the opposite of. Disagree means to not agree.
hint: Which prefix means not?

q: A shark's bite is full of power. Which word means 'full of power'?
why: The suffix -ful means full of. Powerless means without power, which is the opposite.
hint: Which word ending means full of?

q: The baseball team was unbeatable. What is the root word in 'unbeatable'?
why: Take off the prefix un- and the ending -able, and beat is left. The word table is just hiding at the end.
hint: Take off the beginning and the ending.

q: The words 'pair' and 'pear' are homophones.
why: Homophones sound the same but have different spellings and meanings. A pair is two, and a pear is a fruit.
hint: Say both words aloud. Do they sound alike?

q: The shark's teeth were enormous. Which word means almost the same as enormous?
why: Enormous means very, very big, and so does gigantic. Ordinary means normal, and sharp is a different idea.
hint: Choose a word that means very big.

q: Shark skin is as ____ as sandpaper. Which word fits?
why: Coarse means rough. Course is a path or a class. They sound the same but mean different things.
hint: Which word means rough?

q: The batter swung at the first pitch. Which meaning of 'pitch' fits?
opts: how high or low a sound is
a ball thrown by the pitcher
why: Pitch has many meanings. Here a batter is swinging at a ball, so it means the throw.
hint: Use the clue: the batter swung.

q: How many of these words start with the prefix un-: unlock, uncle, undo, under, unfair?
why: Unlock, undo, and unfair add un- to a real word. Uncle and under do not, since cle and der are not words.
hint: Remove un-. Is a real word left?

q: In 'The shark swam silently into the cave,' which word is the adverb?
why: An adverb tells how, when, or where. Silently tells how the shark swam.
hint: Which word tells how it swam?

q: The outfielder ____ the fly ball with one hand. Which word fits?
why: Catch changes to caught in the past. Catched is not a word.
hint: The play already happened.

q: Put these words in order from coldest to hottest.
why: Words can show small or big amounts. Freezing is the coldest, and scorching is the hottest.
hint: Imagine a thermometer rising.

q: The shark circled its prey, a seal swimming near the rocks. What does 'prey' mean?
why: Prey is an animal that other animals hunt and eat. The hunter is called the predator.
hint: What is the shark about to do?

q: In which word do the letters ph make the f sound?
why: In dolphin, ph sounds like f. In uphill, the p and h are separate sounds in different word parts.
hint: Say each word and listen for an f sound.

q: The prefix re- means 'not,' so 'redo' means 'not do.'
why: Re- means again, so redo means do again. The prefix un- is one that means not.
hint: What do you do when you redo a puzzle?

q: The two sharks ____ near the reef every day. Which verb fits?
why: Two sharks is plural, so the verb has no -s. Swims goes with one shark.
hint: Is it one shark or more than one?

q: The root 'aqua' means water. Which word has to do with water?
why: An aquarium holds water and fish. Quarter, equal, and squad only have the letters qua inside them.
hint: Which word names a place with water inside?

q: Dinosaur fossils are ancient. Which word is the opposite of ancient?
why: Ancient means very, very old, so the opposite is modern or new. Old is a synonym.
hint: An opposite means the reverse.

q: The word 'diver' means 'one who dives,' because -er can mean 'one who.'
why: Adding -er to a verb can name the person who does it: dive and diver, teach and teacher.
hint: Think of words like baker and teacher.

q: The word 'astronaut' comes from old words for 'star' and 'sailor.' So an astronaut is a sailor of the ____ .
why: Astro means star and naut means sailor. Astronaut means star sailor.
hint: Think about where astronauts travel.

q: Which sentence uses 'ray' to mean a flat fish that glides through the sea?
opts: A ray of sunshine lit the water.
The coach felt a ray of hope.
A ray glided over the sandy reef.
A ray from the lamp lit the page.
why: A ray can be a fish or a beam of light. Only one sentence is about the animal.
hint: Which sentence is about an animal?

q: Fin is to shark as wing is to ____ .
why: A fin is a part of a shark, and a wing is a part of a bird. A feather is a part of the wing.
hint: Fin is a part of a shark. A wing is part of what?

q: A triceratops had horns on its face. Triangle, tricycle, and triceratops all start with tri-. What does tri- mean?
why: Tri- means three. A triangle has three sides, a tricycle has three wheels, and a triceratops had three horns.
hint: Count the sides of a triangle.

q: After the class show, the teacher said, 'That was a home run!' What did she mean?
why: A home run is the best hit in baseball, so people use it to say something went very well.
hint: Is she talking about a real baseball game?

q: The prefix sub- means 'under,' so a submarine travels under the sea.
why: Sub- means under or below, and marine means of the sea. A submarine travels under the sea.
hint: Marine has to do with the sea.

q: The root 'scope' means to look. Which tool lets you look at stars that are very far away?
why: Tele means far, as in telephone, so a telescope looks at far things. Micro means small.
hint: Tele means far, like in telephone.

q: The shark ____ through the water without a sound. Which word best shows smooth, quiet movement?
why: Glided means moved smoothly and easily. Crashed, stomped, and bounced sound noisy or bumpy.
hint: Pick the word that sounds smooth and quiet.

q: The pitcher was tired, ____ he kept throwing hard. Which word fits best?
why: But shows a contrast: he was tired, yet kept going. So and because show cause and do not fit.
hint: Does the second part go against the first?

q: How many adjectives are in this sentence? Huge, gray whales swam slowly.
why: Huge and gray describe the whales, so they are adjectives. Slowly tells how they swam, so it is an adverb.
hint: Adjectives describe nouns.

q: The word 'dinosaur' comes from the Greek words 'deinos' and 'sauros.' Which meaning matches?
why: Dino means terrible and saur means lizard. Dinosaurs were reptiles, though not true lizards.
hint: Think of words like stegosaurus and lizard.

q: The octopus was camouflaged. It matched the rocks so well that the diver swam right past. What does 'camouflaged' mean?
why: Camouflaged means hidden by looking like the surroundings. The clue is that it matched the rocks.
hint: Use the clue: matched the rocks.

q: A baseball glove that can be washed is washable. What does the suffix -able mean?
why: Washable means able to be washed. The suffix -less means without, and -ful means full of.
hint: Think about what washable says about a glove.

q: Put these windy words in order from the calmest to the strongest.
why: A calm day has no wind. A breeze is light, a gale is strong, and a hurricane is the most powerful.
hint: Imagine wind getting stronger and stronger.

q: The swimmer was pushed along by a strong current. Which meaning of 'current' fits?
why: Here, current means water moving in one direction. It can also mean happening now, or electricity flowing.
hint: Think about what pushes a swimmer.

q: Tall is to short as wide is to ____ .
why: Tall and short are opposites, and so are wide and narrow.
hint: Find the opposite of wide.

q: Which group of words is a complete sentence?
why: A sentence needs a subject and a verb, and it must make sense alone. The other groups leave something out.
hint: Which one tells who did what?

q: It is correct to say 'less sharks' because less is the word for things you can count.
why: Use fewer for things you can count, like fewer sharks. Use less for amounts, like less water.
hint: Can you count sharks one by one?

q: In 'The submarine glided beneath the waves,' which word is the preposition?
why: A preposition shows where something is. Beneath tells where the submarine glided.
hint: Which word tells where?

q: Seeing one fin was just the tip of the iceberg; many sharks were nearby. What does 'tip of the iceberg' mean?
opts: a small part of something bigger
a very cold and icy place
a smart way to stay safe
a rare and very lucky chance
why: Most of an iceberg hides underwater. The saying means you see just a small part of something much bigger.
hint: Think of how much of an iceberg you cannot see.

q: A very faint star may not be ____ without a telescope. Which spelling is correct?
why: Visible ends in -ible, not -able. Memory trick: if you can see it with your vision, it is visible.
hint: The word starts like vision.

q: The word 'than' is used to compare things, as in 'The Moon is smaller than Earth.'
why: Than compares two things. Then tells about time, as in first this, then that.
hint: Think of words that compare, like bigger than.

q: The root 'aud' means to hear. A whale's song can be ____ from far away. Which word fits?
why: Audible means able to be heard. Visible is for seeing, edible for eating, and legible for reading.
hint: Think of an audience, which listens.

q: All the players ____ Sam got to practice on time. Which word fits?
why: Except means leaving out. Accept means to take or agree to something.
hint: Which word means everyone but Sam?

q: Which sentence uses 'wind' with the long-i sound, as in 'find'?
opts: A cold wind blew across the bay.
why: When wind means to twist or turn, it rhymes with find. The wind that blows rhymes with pinned.
hint: Which wind is something you do to a toy?

q: The word 'lead,' the metal, sounds exactly like 'led,' the past tense of 'lead.'
why: The metal is said 'led.' So the two words sound alike, even though they are spelled differently.
hint: Say the metal's name out loud.

q: The root 'port' means to carry. Which word means 'able to be carried'?
why: Port means carry and -able means can be. A porter is a person who carries, not a thing that can be carried.
hint: Add the ending that means can be.

q: 'The Moon was a silver coin hanging in the sky.' Which figure of speech is this?
why: A metaphor says one thing is another, without like or as. A simile would say the Moon was like a coin.
hint: Does it use the word like or as?

q: Crabs live in the intertidal zone. The prefix inter- means 'between.' Where is this zone?
opts: far out in the deep sea
why: Intertidal means between the tides. It is the shore that is covered at high tide and bare at low tide.
hint: Tidal has to do with tides.

q: How many compound words are in this list: starfish, dolphin, seahorse, jellyfish, octopus, sailboat?
why: Starfish, seahorse, jellyfish, and sailboat are each two words joined. Dolphin and octopus are not.
hint: Can you split the word into two real words?

q: Which sentence is an exaggeration (hyperbole)?
opts: I'm so hungry I could eat a whale.
I'm hungry after the long game.
The pitcher was hungry for a win.
We ate lunch after the game.
why: Hyperbole stretches the truth so far that no one believes it. Nobody could really eat a whale.
hint: Which one could not possibly be true?

q: The word 'tsunami' comes from the Japanese words 'tsu' and 'nami.' What do they mean together?
why: Tsu means harbor and nami means wave. A tsunami is a giant wave that can crash into a harbor.
hint: One part names a place where boats stay.

q: A shark may ____ many teeth in its life. Which word fits?
why: Lose is a verb that means to no longer have something. Loose means not tight.
hint: You need the verb meaning to not keep.

q: Put these words in ABC order. Check each letter in turn.
why: All start with pla. Plate has t fourth, so it goes last. For the others, the fifth letter decides: e, then k, then t.
hint: Find the first letter where the words differ.

q: Tired is to exhausted as hungry is to ____ .
why: Exhausted means extremely tired. Starving means extremely hungry. Both pairs go from mild to very strong.
hint: Find the very strong word for hungry.

q: A writer describes a graceful dolphin. Which word has the most positive feeling?
why: Words with similar meanings can feel different. Slender sounds graceful; scrawny and bony sound weak.
hint: Which word would you like said about you?

q: Which sentence joins its two thoughts correctly?
opts: The ball flew so, fans cheered.
The ball flew. so fans cheered.
The ball flew, so fans cheered.
why: Two full thoughts need more than a comma. A comma plus so joins them correctly.
hint: Two full sentences need a joining word.

q: Telescope is to planet as microscope is to ____ .
why: A telescope shows faraway things like planets. A microscope shows tiny things like cells.
hint: Which tool shows tiny things?

q: 'The shark is a torpedo with teeth' is a simile.
why: A simile compares using like or as. This says the shark is a torpedo, so it is a metaphor.
hint: Look for the words like or as.

q: A jellyfish injects toxin when it stings. Which word describes it most exactly?
why: Venomous animals inject toxin with a bite or sting. Poisonous ones are harmful to eat or touch.
hint: The clue word is injects.

q: The word 'bass' can name a fish or a deep musical sound. How is the deep sound said?
why: The fish rhymes with class. The deep sound rhymes with face. The spelling is the same but the sound differs.
hint: Think of a bass guitar.

q: Which of these words came from a person's name?
why: The sandwich is named for the Earl of Sandwich. Sunrise, seashell, and sailboat are made of two plain words.
hint: Which word is not two simple words?

q: The root 'rupt' means to break. Which word means to break in on someone's talking?
why: Inter- means between, so interrupt means to break in between. Erupt means to burst out, and abrupt means sudden.
hint: Which prefix means between?

q: Geologist is to rocks as astronomer is to ____ .
why: A geologist studies rocks, and an astronomer studies stars and planets. Fossils belong to a paleontologist.
hint: What does an astronomer study?

q: The root 'chron' means time. Which word describes events listed in the order they happened?
why: Chronological means in time order. Chronic means lasting a long time. Chromatic comes from the word for color.
hint: Think of a timeline.

q: The word 'ambiguous' means 'having only one clear meaning.'
why: Ambiguous means unclear or open to more than one meaning. A word with one clear meaning is unambiguous.
hint: Think about what un-ambiguous would mean.

q: A reporter keeps asking the pitcher many questions. Which word would sound like a complaint?
why: Nosy has a negative feeling, as if the questions are unwanted. The other words sound positive or neutral.
hint: Which word would the pitcher not enjoy hearing?

q: The root 'pisc' means fish and -vore means eater. Which animal is a piscivore?
opts: a cow grazing in a field
why: A piscivore is a fish eater. The cow, bee, and koala eat grass, nectar, and leaves.
hint: Put the two word parts together: fish eater.

q: The singular is 'alga,' a simple organism that includes seaweed. What is the plural?
why: Alga comes from Latin, and its plural is algae, said AL-jee. Most English plurals add -s, but this one does not.
hint: Latin words often change their endings.

q: How many syllables are in the word 'paleontologist'?
why: Pa-le-on-tol-o-gist has six beats. The middle part, on-tol-o, is easy to miss.
hint: Clap slowly and watch the vowels in the middle.

q: The school ____ cheered for the baseball team. Which spelling is correct?
why: A principal is the head of a school. Memory trick: the principal is your pal. A principle is a rule.
hint: Which word means the head of a school?

q: Which sentence uses 'fast' as an adverb?
opts: The mako is a fast swimmer.
why: An adverb tells how an action happens. Fast tells how the mako swims. In the others, fast describes a noun.
hint: Does fast describe a noun or an action?

q: The word 'umpire' once began with n: 'a noumpere.' People heard it as 'an oumpere.' What happened to the n?
opts: It slid onto the word before it
It was replaced by a u
It was lost in a spelling contest
why: People heard 'a noumpere' as 'an oumpere,' so the n joined the article. Apron was once 'napron' the same way.
hint: Say 'a noumpere' quickly out loud.

q: Put these words in ABC order. They all start with kn.
why: Skip the shared kn and compare the third letters: a, e, i, o, u. The vowels go in that order.
hint: The third letter is the first one that differs.

q: Chilly is to frigid as damp is to ____ .
why: Frigid is a much stronger word than chilly. Soaked is a much stronger word than damp.
hint: Find the very strong word for damp.

q: The astronomer was meticulous. She checked every measurement of the star three times. What does 'meticulous' mean?
why: The clue is that she checked every measurement three times. Meticulous means extremely careful about details.
hint: Use the clue: checked three times.

q: Which sentence uses 'sound' to mean a stretch of sea water between pieces of land?
opts: A loud sound woke the crew.
The boat crossed the sound at dawn.
The old pier is safe and sound.
Sound the alarm if you see fins.
why: A sound can be a stretch of sea between lands, like Puget Sound. The other sentences use other meanings.
hint: Which sentence is about water and land?

q: The word 'disaster' comes from old words that mean 'bad star.'
why: Dis- means bad and astro means star. Long ago, people blamed bad events on the stars.
hint: Think of astro in astronaut.

q: Each of the players ____ a glove on the bench. Which verb fits?
why: Each is singular, even with 'of the players' after it. So use has.
hint: Each means one at a time.

q: Seaweed was abundant on the beach after the storm. Which word is the best opposite of abundant?
why: Abundant means more than enough. Scarce means hard to find. Plentiful and common mean the same as abundant.
hint: Which word means hard to find?

q: The tenacious pitcher kept trying even after walking five batters. What does 'tenacious' mean?
why: Tenacious means holding on and refusing to quit. The clue is that he kept trying after hard moments.
hint: Use the clue: kept trying.

q: 'A rising tide lifts all boats.' What does this saying mean?
why: The saying is figurative. When the tide rises, every boat rises. So when things get better, everyone gains.
hint: Is it about real boats or a bigger idea?
